title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 10): The old man and the Seethe
summary: Part 10 of NH's long mocking series about a YouTube strength coach he nicknames 'Blojo'. He presents what he calls proof of fake calibrated and bumper plates, mocks the man's drama with other YouTubers, claimed FFMI, powerlifting credentials, age excuses and lifestyle, and argues he is a failed bodybuilder who covets aesthetics. Along the way he gives his own views on pound-for-pound strength, age, form and the strength community.
claims: He alleges the YouTuber uses fake Rogue calibrated plates bought from China, betrayed by a missing deep ridge on the back and plates that swing like they weigh 5 lb on pull-ups
Claiming an FFMI of 28 (above Arnold and Serge Nubret) while visibly fat shows how badly people underestimate their body fat
Fat on the thighs isn't muscle; claiming 30-inch thighs from fat is like claiming the best six-pack because of a big gut
Successful content should be spared instead of milked until the audience loses interest
Coaching clients to good-morning with a rounded back and calling it learning to strain is destroying their spines
Slamming the bar onto pins and squatting it up through a quarter range is a pin quarter squat, not a good morning, for strength or size
Placing at a local meet often automatically qualifies you for worlds in some federations; it's a fee-paying business, not an elite invitation
A world record is only broken in competition, and backyard meets lack legitimacy
Pound-for-pound strength matters; top sub-200 lb powerlifters agree, otherwise big frames that can bulk to huge numbers have too much advantage
Powerlifting has shifted, even in top classes, from packing on mass to carrying heavy lean muscle, for efficiency and health
Lifters stuck between cutting for looks and bulking to keep strength lose and gain the same 10 lb forever without progress
Naturals should peak in strength and aesthetics in their 30s and 40s; using age as an excuse in your 40s is a cope
You should stay mobile until about 80; bodies beaten down in their 40s come from lifting badly, not from lifting itself
In this community he respects only strength and size; veterans with neither shouldn't demand respect for years in the game
Poor posture (a hunched back) affects the way you lift
People who get laid don't feel the need to talk about it; constant bragging is a sign of lying
Calories are fuel for strength or muscle; a big appetite that just stores fat on the couch is nothing to brag about
He blames this YouTuber for starting much of the toxicity on YouTube fitness: supplement bashing, then his own supplement line, drama videos
